correctness.rationale: For a chain-ring factor of nilpotency length \(\ell\), valuation \(a\) has annihilator at complementary valuation \(\ell-a\). Thus product-ring annihilator classes are exactly valuation vectors, and two distinct classes are adjacent exactly when every coordinate sum reaches its local nilpotency length. For each factor, the vector \(w_i\) supported by valuation one in that coordinate has the unique neighbor \(d_i\), forcing all \(d_i\) into every total dominating set. The \(d_i\) form a clique and dominate all vertices. Paired domination then follows from the even-cardinality requirement and an explicit matching. The local one-factor case is checked separately. The standalone verifier exhaustively checks representative parameter boxes and independently rebuilds several product rings from multiplication tables.

originality.rationale: Prior work covers the definition and structure of the compressed graph, ordinary domination of the compressed graph, and total domination of the ordinary zero-divisor graph. The inspected full texts and targeted searches did not state the forced minimum total core, its uniqueness, the paired-domination parity formula, or the classification and count of all minimum paired sets for finite commutative principal ideal rings. Ordinary domination number equal to the number of local factors is explicitly treated as prior coverage, not as part of the novelty claim.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete classification of total and paired domination for all nonfield finite commutative PIRs, including the exact local obstruction. For nonlocal rings it identifies a canonical forced core indexed by local factors, proves uniqueness of the minimum total set, determines the paired parity correction, classifies every minimum paired set, and counts them. These conclusions are structurally stronger than the known ordinary domination value and provide graph-visible information about the local decomposition.
